system.summary: Code words mixed with clear English words. 1922: ordinary English words used as code. 1923-24: words of several languages of the kind in the Berne official vocabulary of 1901 (ASEGURABAN, COLLIGAREM, VERLANDEN...) and some artificial or garbled ten-letter words; ANZUNDET in both. 1916: two code names. Book not identified.

prior_solution.where: Only the two 1916 code names are glossed in pencil on the form. No decoding of the 1922-24 telegrams on the leaves, in the Senate oil-lease hearings, DECODE or Lasry's list (vetting 13 Nov 2026, PR #580).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (criterion fixed and hashed before decoding). An AI agent transcribed, screened the code books and wrote the sheets. No human check of the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: IIIF images of the four telegrams fetched with curl at native size (1500 px).
Full transcription, two passes, the second blind on enlarged crops; the passes agree; word totals match the operators' counts (42, 96, 30); three overstrikes left open.

Code book screening: exact match of the code words in the OCR of 23 commercial codes on archive.org, criterion fixed beforehand (>= 90% coverage, then coherent decoding). Best 6/67 (1923-24) and 6/12 (1922); Western Union 1901 and McNeill 1908 checked by hand and ruled out.

Position of the code words in the clear frame: ANZUNDET after FOR twice (a place); ARROGANCE after days and hours (a time word); the 1923 telegram a quoted document with numbered paragraphs. Not decoded.

validation.notes: No book passed the coverage criterion, so no decoding was measured.

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: 79 of 168 words of the three coded telegrams are clear words; 0 of 89 code words decoded.
